decisions.question: Will the percent of Pakistanis in extreme poverty be above 5 percent in 2023?
decisions.thinking: With the 2018 extreme poverty baseline at 4.93%, even a minimal increase crosses the 5% threshold. The 2022 floods combined with historic 30%+ inflation in 2022-2023 severely eroded purchasing power at the bottom deciles, driving broad poverty metrics up across World Bank reporting.
decisions.uncertainty: Whether the specific $2.15/day international extreme poverty metric in World Bank PIP / OWID for 2023 will capture the full real-income loss from 2022-2023 food inflation.
decisions.resolution_risk: Data availability delay leading to market extension, or methodology shifts in OWID's default displayed line.
evidence_for: Baseline extreme poverty ($2.15/day PPP) in 2018 was 4.93%, leaving a margin of only 0.07 percentage points below the 5% threshold.
Pakistan experienced catastrophic flooding in 2022 affecting over 33 million people, followed by hyperinflation exceeding 30-40% for basic food items in 2022-2023.
World Bank data confirms substantial poverty increases across all measured thresholds in FY23, with the $3.65 lower-middle-income line jumping from 34.2% to 39.4% and national poverty reaching 25.3%.
